common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Cervical Radiculopathy.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to peripheral entrapment neuropathy without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Progressive motor weakness, gait disturbance, or bowel/bladder dysfunction suggesting myelopathy.

teaching.one_liner: Cervical nerve-root compression causing neck pain radiating to the arm with dermatomal sensory symptoms, reflex changes, and focal weakness.
red_flags: Progressive arm weakness or loss of hand function
Gait imbalance or bowel/bladder dysfunction suggesting cervical myelopathy

must_ask.say: Does the neck pain travel into your shoulder, arm, thumb, or index finger?
Does turning or extending your neck make the arm pain or tingling worse?
Have you developed hand clumsiness, trouble walking, or bowel or bladder changes?
Does looking up or turning your head toward the painful side reproduce the arm symptoms?
Have you noticed weakness when lifting, bending your elbow, extending your wrist, or gripping?
